To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an approach that uses ontological representation of biophysical dependencies to enable computational analysis of biophysical models.
we have developed an ontology of physical properties, processes and dependencies that are used to represent and reason about biophysical knowledge.
we have developed a formal, computational ontology of the physical dependencies of biophysical processes that are the basis of the mathematical analysis of physiological systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with

representing the biophysical semantics of mathematical statements and models of biological processes and the development of computational tools for the creation, representation, and querying of such formal knowledge.
representing and reasoning about the meaning of biophysical models and datasets in a manner that is computable, reusable, and interoperable.
the formalization of the meaning of mathematical statements of physiological processes and their representations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we are developing a formalized representation of the meaning of the mathematics that is used to describe physiological processes.

our ontology of physics for biology is a computational ontology that represents the laws of physics as dependencies between physical properties and physical entities that occur in biological processes.
the OPB is an ontology that provides a formal, computational representation of biophysical knowledge for the analysis and simulation of physiological processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are developing an ontological framework to represent the biophysical content and semantics of biosimulations and the biophysical knowledge they encode.
we are developing a formal representation of the biophysics of physiological processes that can be used for knowledge representation, model analysis, and model simulation in the VPH and VPR.
OPB is a “physiology ontology” for the representation of the biophysical meaning of mathematical analysis and modeling of physiological processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are able to use a computational ontology to represent the meaning of the mathematical statements of biophysical analysis.
we have shown that it is possible to represent the semantics of mathematical statements in a way that is compatible with the representation of physical properties and processes.
the laws of classical and statistical physics provide the basis for a unified, formal representation of biophysical processes that can be applied in a variety of computational contexts.
